s.t: The Staple Singers' single spent three weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot Soul Singles chart in 1973 and became a gold record.
s.src: If You're Ready (Come Go with Me) - Wikipedia
s.q: the single spent three weeks at number one on the Billboard magazine's Hot Soul Singles chart in 1973.  It peaked at number nine on the Billboard Hot 100 pop singles chart.  It became a gold record.

s.t: Mavis Staples worried that the Staple Singers' song sounded too close to their previous hit, ‘I'll Take You There’.
s.q: Mavis worried the song was too close to their last hit.

f.t: Their song ‘Uncloudy Day’ was an early influence on Bob Dylan, who said in 2015 that Mavis Staples's singing "just knocked me out".
f.q: "Uncloudy Day" was an early influence on Bob Dylan, who said of it in 2015 ... Her singing just knocked me out

f.t: Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples worked in steel mills and meatpacking plants in Chicago while his children grew up, before the family began singing in local churches in 1948.
f.q: Roebuck worked in steel mills and meatpacking plants while his family of four children grew up. The family began appearing in Chicago-area churches in 1948.

f.t: They performed ‘The Weight’ with The Band in the film The Last Waltz in 1976, having covered the song on their first Stax album.
f.q: In 1976, they collaborated with The Band for their film The Last Waltz, performing on the song "The Weight" (which The Staple Singers had previously covered on their first Stax album).

f.t: Their 1984 cover of Talking Heads' ‘Slippery People’ reached the Top 5 on the Dance chart.
f.q: The 1984 album Turning Point featured a cover of Talking Heads' "Slippery People", which reached the Top 5 on the Dance chart.
